# Contributing

## Run it in 30 seconds — no key, no signup, no install

```bash
git clone https://github.com/edycutjong/forwarding.git && cd forwarding
python3 scripts/forwarding.py investigate --platform ethereum --address 0x1f9840a85d5af5bf1d1762f925bdaddc4201f984
```

`forwarding.py` is stdlib-only and every endpoint it calls is on CoinMarketCap's keyless
`/public-api` surface, so what you see is a live investigation, not a fixture.

## Development

```bash
make setup           # dev deps only (pytest, pytest-cov, hypothesis, ruff, mypy, pip-audit)
make lint            # ruff check + format check
make typecheck       # mypy over scripts/ and api/
make test            # offline tests, no internet
make test-coverage   # the same, with coverage of every file in scripts/ and api/ gated at 100%
make test-live       # the tests that hit the real CoinMarketCap API and the deployment
make demo            # the judged capability, live, no key
make bench           # p50/p95 of adjudicate() over the committed receipts (deterministic)
make bench-live      # p50/p95 of a real keyless investigation
make site            # re-render site/index.html, site/judge.html and JUDGE.md from docs/proof/*.json
make verify          # replay every receipt through the invariants, check chain of custody
make check           # refuse to ship a placeholder, a stale count or a drifted page
make audit           # pip-audit + gitleaks
make ci              # lint typecheck test-coverage verify check audit
```

## The one rule that matters here

**Never mock the judged capability.** The point of this project is that the verdict comes from
real liquidity events with real maker addresses. If a test needs determinism, route a
`FakeClient` (tests/conftest.py) whose rows have the exact shape the live endpoint returns —
but the default path, `make demo`, and CI's `live-api` job must always hit the real API. A pull
request that puts the investigation behind a mock flag will be closed.

`scripts/bench.py --replay` and `scripts/verify.py` are the sanctioned offline paths, and both
are labelled a replay everywhere they appear. They measure the arithmetic, not the product.

## Numbers are rendered, never typed

`site/index.html`, `site/judge.html` and `JUDGE.md` are generated by `scripts/render_site.py`
from the receipts in `docs/proof/`. Edit the template in `scripts/site_templates/` or re-capture
the receipt (`make seed`, `make base-rate`, `make bench-live`), then `make site`. Editing the
rendered files by hand fails `make check`. The test counts the README and DEMO state are
checked against `pytest --collect-only` by the same gate.

## Tests

Three categories carry more weight than coverage here, and PRs are expected to keep them:

- **Regression tests are named after the defect they pin**, with the date it was seen live in
  the docstring — `test_a_usd_value_larger_than_every_market_on_earth_is_a_price_artefact_not_a_removal`,
  not `test_filter_3`. The test list is meant to read as a changelog of real bugs.
- **`adjudicate()` is verified by property, not by example** (`tests/test_property.py`,
  2,000 generated investigations). If you change the rule, invariants I1–I6 in `docs/SPEC.md`
  must still hold across the input space, and the thresholds in the test must match the spec.
- **The boundaries are tested, not described** (`tests/test_boundary.py`): no MCP tool can be
  made to send data anywhere or take a credential; the hosted proxy accepts exactly a chain slug
  and an EVM address and follows the same chain only.

Live tests (`pytest -m live`) assert the outside world — that `maker=` really filters, that the
committed hero reproduces from a fresh fetch, that the deployment holds no key. A 429 from the
anonymous tier is reported as a skip with CMC's message, never as a pass.

## Commits

Conventional commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`, `test:`, `ci:`, `style:`). Small and
iterative. `release.yml` derives the version from these, so the prefix decides the version bump.
